notes: S5-HVS1 is cited only as a possible example of the paper's predicted hypervelocity-star population; the paper does not newly measure its boundness. It is treated as follow_up because it is described as a previously discovered object ejected from the Galactic Center (T:p17-b3), while the paper states that the HVS will escape the Galaxy (T:p11-b7). No Gaia identifier is supplied.

S5-HVS1: The only mention of S5-HVS1 is in T:p17-b3 (and a repeated generic reference in the abstract/summary about hyper-velocity stars): "A possible example is the recently discovered object S5-HVS1, which was ejected from our Galactic Center about 5 Myr ago at an inferred velocity of v_∞ ≃ 1800 km s^-1 (Koposov et al. 2020)." This value is the star's asymptotic ejection velocity (speed at infinity), not a heliocentric/barycentric line-of-sight velocity nor a total three-dimensional speed in the Galactic rest frame, and the paper reports no position, distance, parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability for this object. No eligible quantity can therefore be extracted.
